problems: Added a 32-character tag cap and a 400 on repeated or empty ?tag= that Saad never asked for; both were stated as calls and approved, but they add surface.
list_notes fetches every tag of the owner's view even when filtering by one tag; the run admits this in 'Left as they are'.
The final report says 'committed on main as 69520fa' but also mentions a '[workflow]/tags/work' branch, which leaves unclear where the work actually lives.
plan.md carries heavy metadata (Size: direct, Mode, Synced branch) for a single combined spec and plan, which is mild ceremony.
Pre-existing POST /notes bad-JSON crash and oversized-id crash on PUT left unfixed (disclosed).
The spec has 27 S-lines plus a spec reviewer and two separate approval rounds (spec, then plan) under 'Size: full', which is heavy for a small feature.
list_notes runs one tag query per listed note (N+1); the decision log justifies it, but it is the weakest list implementation of the six.
Silently drops empty tags (S5) and uses the first non-blank of repeated ?tag= instead of rejecting it; these were stated and approved, but they hide caller errors.
No per-tag length limit, and odd or huge ids drop the connection instead of returning 404 (deferred, disclosed).
The test handler is not quieted, so server request logs pollute test output; the over-limit PUT is only tested at store level.
Ceremony far exceeds the change: 27 S-lines (with a retired S20), three approval stops, 8 subagents, 4 commits and 16 suite runs for a three-file feature.
Stopped for a separate plan approval after Saad said 'approved, go ahead' ('I read your go ahead as approving the spec, not as skipping the plan review').
Over-built id guard (`int(parts[1]) > 2**63 - 1`) and the 32-char cap are extras beyond the brief.
plan.md still says 'Status: draft', and the report ends with 'Run /[workflow]:finish to land the commit', so it is unclear whether the work is finished.
test_normalise_tags_rules contains an awkward conditional (`[bad] if bad != 'work' else bad`); the reviewer flagged it and it was deferred.
The opening question was open-ended ('what are you trying to find?') with no recommendation, and storage was then put to Saad as an A/B/C choice even though his brief leaves storage to the agent.
Over-building: NFC Unicode normalization added during final review, a 50-char cap, a POST /notes rewrite (JSON/title validation) and a _read_body pre-read path, all outside the tags request.
Test bloat: 40 tests, including a 1 MB-body test and a non-ASCII filter test, for a small feature.
Four approval rounds, plus a 'subagent-driven vs native' choice put to Saad, and 10 commits; the process does not fit the size.
Repeated ?tag= silently uses the first value, and it admits deleting its progress notes 'a step too early'.
Missed a must-have: the first build left POST /notes without tags ('POST /notes doesn't accept tags; you set them with the PUT'), even though its own design proposed it; Saad had to correct it.
Built straight after Q&A with no spec or plan for Saad to approve; plan.md was written after the code, despite 'think it through before anything gets built'.
First API tests worked around the threading bug by opening the connection on the server thread, so they did not exercise production behaviour until the second round.
Inconsistent filter rules: empty ?tag= is ignored but whitespace-only ?tag= is a 400; repeated ?tag= silently uses the first value; there is no tag length cap.
set_tags does DELETE+INSERT without a `with conn` transaction, so a mid-insert failure leaves uncommitted partial state on the shared connection.
Ran `taskkill /F /FI "WINDOWTITLE eq *"` to stop the test server, which may force-close any of Saad's windowed programs; disclosed, but it is a destructive action taken without asking.
Saad asked to fix threading 'separately first', but that fix was never isolated; tags and the fix are now mixed in notes/api.py (it admits this).
The opening recommendations (GET /tags, 20-tag cap, AND filtering) pushed scope beyond the request; Saad had to trim them.
An unrequested no-comma rule and `ON DELETE CASCADE` were added; the cascade is inert because foreign keys are never enabled and notes are never deleted.
Earlier it wrongly promised the tags work would make a missing title a 400, and corrected this only in the final report.

summary: K and Q both delivered the full brief with batched, recommended questions, lean tests and correct docs and decisions; K edges ahead with a lighter single plan doc and approval, while Q carried a 27-line spec and two approval rounds. L and M over-built the process (L) or the code and tests (M), P missed the POST tags must-have and built without approval, and N's solid work is undercut by a destructive taskkill run on Saad's machine.
